# Nat (Resource)

Manages a source NAT rule: the controller rewrites the address of traffic leaving a WAN interface, most commonly masquerading a network behind the WAN's own address.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination_filter` (Attributes) Which traffic the rule matches on its destination address and port. Leave `filter_type` at `NONE` to match any destination. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination_filter))
- `protocol` (String) The protocol the rule matches: `all`, `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`. The controller requires this on every write.
- `source_filter` (Attributes) Which traffic the rule matches on its source address and port. Leave `filter_type` at `NONE` to match any source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source_filter))

### Optional

- `description` (String) A human-readable description of the NAT rule.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled.
- `in_interface` (String) The inbound interface the rule matches on. Usually left unset for a source NAT rule.
- `ip_address` (String) The address traffic is translated to. Empty for `MASQUERADE`, which uses the outbound interface's own address.
- `ip_version` (String) The IP version the rule applies to: `IPV4` or `IPV6`.
- `logging` (Boolean) Whether traffic the rule matches is logged.
- `out_interface` (String) The outbound interface the rule masquerades on: the `_id` of a WAN `unifi_network`, not the literal `wan`.
- `port` (Number) The translated port, for a `DNAT` rule that also rewrites the port.
- `setting_preference` (String) Whether the controller orders the rule automatically (`auto`) or honours `rule_index` (`manual`).
- `site` (String) The name of the site the NAT rule belongs to.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `type` (String) The kind of NAT the rule performs: `DNAT`, `SNAT` or `MASQUERADE`.

### Read-Only

- `exclude` (Boolean) Whether the rule excludes rather than includes the matched traffic. Controller-managed.
- `id` (String) The ID of the NAT rule.
- `is_predefined` (Boolean) Whether the rule is one the controller ships. Controller-managed.
- `pppoe_use_base_interface` (Boolean) Whether a PPPoE outbound interface masquerades on its base interface. Controller-managed.
- `rule_index` (Number) The rule's position in the controller's evaluation order. Controller-assigned.

<a id="nestedatt--destination_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination_filter`

Optional:

- `address` (String) The destination address or CIDR to match when `filter_type` is `ADDRESS_AND_PORT`.
- `filter_type` (String) How the destination is matched: `NONE`, `ADDRESS_AND_PORT`, `FIREWALL_GROUPS` or `NETWORK_CONF`.
- `firewall_group_ids` (List of String) IDs of the `unifi_firewall_group`s to match when `filter_type` is `FIREWALL_GROUPS`.
- `invert_address` (Boolean) Match every destination except the one described, rather than only it.
- `invert_port` (Boolean) Match every destination port except the one described, rather than only it.
- `network_conf_id` (String) ID of the `unifi_network` to match when `filter_type` is `NETWORK_CONF`.
- `port` (Number) The destination port to match when `filter_type` is `ADDRESS_AND_PORT`.


<a id="nestedatt--source_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source_filter`

Optional:

- `address` (String) The source address or CIDR to match when `filter_type` is `ADDRESS_AND_PORT`.
- `filter_type` (String) How the source is matched: `NONE`, `ADDRESS_AND_PORT`, `FIREWALL_GROUPS` or `NETWORK_CONF`.
- `firewall_group_ids` (List of String) IDs of the `unifi_firewall_group`s to match when `filter_type` is `FIREWALL_GROUPS`.
- `invert_address` (Boolean) Match every source except the one described, rather than only it.
- `invert_port` (Boolean) Match every source port except the one described, rather than only it.
- `network_conf_id` (String) ID of the `unifi_network` to match when `filter_type` is `NETWORK_CONF`.
- `port` (Number) The source port to match when `filter_type` is `ADDRESS_AND_PORT`.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
